newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO PRESIDENT SUSPENDED BY FIFA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO PRESIDENT SUSPENDED BY FIFA.

text.p: FIFA have suspended Deportivo Coruna president Augusto Cesar Lendoiro from all club and soccer activity until August 1998 as punishment for taking the Spanish Football Association to civil court, officials said on Thursday.
Lendoiro was also fined 100,000 Swiss francs ($70,100) for making "defamatory remarks" about FIFA and the Spanish F.A.
By taking the Spanish association to court, Lendoiro was in direct violation of FIFA bylaws which forbid teams from seeking recourse in civil courts.
Lendoiro incurred the world soccer body's wrath when he successfully obtained a court injunction against a one-game home ban imposed by the Spanish F.A.
The incident that sparked the row occured when a referee was hit by a coin during a league match in Coruna last October.
The Spanish federation banned Deportivo from playing their next game -- a sell-out cup clash with Barcelona -- at home.
Deportivo took the Spanish F.A. to court, obtained an injunction, and proceeded with the match.
The club have since ignored FIFA demands to observe the one-match ban.
